front: Which access modifier restricts a member so only code in its own class can use it, not even a subclass?
back: private
accepted_answers: private
hint: It hides implementation details from every class except the declaring one, including subclasses.

front: Which keyword makes a local variable's value unable to be reassigned after initialization?
back: final
accepted_answers: final
hint: It also prevents a class from being subclassed or a method from being overridden.

front: Which functional interface represents an operation that takes no arguments and returns a value?
back: Supplier
accepted_answers: Supplier
hint: Its single abstract method is get().

front: What is the key structural difference between an abstract class and an interface that has default methods?
back: An abstract class can declare instance fields and constructors to hold shared state, while an interface, even with default methods, cannot declare instance fields, so it can only describe behavior.
accepted_answers: abstract classes can hold instance state and constructors; interfaces cannot hold instance fields
hint: Ask whether the type needs constructors or per-instance fields.

front: Why does overriding equals() without overriding hashCode() break lookups in a HashMap or HashSet?
back: Equal objects would be allowed to produce different hash codes, so they could be stored in different buckets and the collection could no longer find a stored key by an equal instance.
accepted_answers: equal objects could hash to different buckets so lookups fail
hint: Hash-based collections locate a bucket by hash code before checking equality.

front: How does method overloading differ from method overriding at resolution time?
back: Overloading is resolved at compile time based on the declared argument types, while overriding is resolved at runtime based on the actual object's class.
accepted_answers: overloading resolved at compile time by parameter types; overriding resolved at runtime by actual object type
hint: One is static dispatch, the other is dynamic dispatch.

front: Why is composition often preferred over implementation inheritance for reusing behavior across classes?
back: Composition reuses behavior by holding a reference to another object instead of extending its class, which avoids fragile base class problems and keeps hierarchies shallow and easier to change.
accepted_answers: avoids fragile base class problems and keeps hierarchies shallow
hint: Ask yourself is-a versus has-a.

front: What is the fundamental difference between a checked exception and an unchecked exception in Java?
back: A checked exception extends Exception (not RuntimeException) and the compiler forces callers to catch or declare it, while an unchecked exception extends RuntimeException and is not enforced by the compiler.
accepted_answers: checked extends Exception and is compiler-enforced; unchecked extends RuntimeException and is not enforced
hint: Think about what the compiler forces you to handle.

front: What is the output of: Integer a = 127, b = 127; System.out.println(a == b);
back: true
accepted_answers: true
hint: Integer caches boxed values from -128 to 127 inclusive.

front: What is the output of: Integer a = 200, b = 200; System.out.println(a == b);
back: false
accepted_answers: false
hint: Values outside the Integer cache range box to distinct objects.

front: What is the output of: String s = null; System.out.println(s + "!");
back: null!
accepted_answers: null!
hint: String concatenation converts a null reference to the text null.

front: A subclass overrides a method that reads one of its own fields, and the superclass constructor calls that overridable method. What value does the overridden method see for the subclass field?
back: It sees the field's default value (0, false, or null) because the subclass's field initializers have not run yet when the superclass constructor executes.
accepted_answers: the field's default value because subclass initializers have not run yet
hint: Subclass initialization happens after the superclass constructor body.

front: A NullPointerException is thrown by user.getAddress().getCity() for only some users in production. What is the most likely root cause?
back: Some user records have a null address reference, so the chained call fails for those records; the code needs a null check or Optional handling before accessing city.
accepted_answers: some users have a null address so the chained call fails
hint: Chained calls fail at the first null link, not necessarily the last method name.

front: Two threads increment a shared plain long counter with no volatile, atomic, or lock, and the final total is consistently lower than the number of increments performed. What is the root cause?
back: Incrementing is a non-atomic read-modify-write sequence, so interleaved updates from different threads can overwrite each other and lose increments.
accepted_answers: increment is non-atomic so interleaved updates overwrite each other and lose increments
hint: Read, add one, and write back are three separate steps.

front: An object is inserted into a HashSet, then a field used in its equals() and hashCode() is mutated, and afterward contains() with an equal-looking object returns false. What is the root cause?
back: The object's hash code changed after it was placed in the set, so it is now searched for in the wrong bucket and can no longer be found even though an equal-looking instance exists.
accepted_answers: hash code changed after insertion so it is searched for in the wrong bucket
hint: Mutable fields used in equals or hashCode should not change after insertion into a hash-based collection.

front: Removing a try/catch around a call causes a compile error for one exception type but not for a RuntimeException thrown by another call in the same block. Why does only one method force error handling?
back: The method throws a checked exception, which the compiler requires callers to catch or declare, while RuntimeException and its subclasses are unchecked and are not enforced by the compiler.
accepted_answers: one throws a checked exception which the compiler enforces; RuntimeException is unchecked and not enforced
hint: Check whether the thrown type extends Exception or RuntimeException.

front: A recursive method that works fine on small inputs throws StackOverflowError only on production-sized inputs. What is the most direct fix?
back: Convert the recursion to an iterative implementation (or manage an explicit stack), since Java does not guarantee tail-call optimization and deep recursion consumes call-stack frames proportional to input size.
accepted_answers: convert to an iterative implementation since Java does not optimize tail calls
hint: Each recursive call keeps its own stack frame until it returns.

front: Write a regular expression that matches a simple email address of the form local@domain.tld, using only word characters, dots, plus, or hyphen before the @, and a 2+ letter top-level domain.
hint: Anchor both ends and escape the literal dot before the top-level domain.

front: Write a try-with-resources statement that opens a BufferedReader over a FileReader for "data.txt" and prints its first line.
back: try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader("data.txt"))) { System.out.println(reader.readLine()); }
accepted_answers: try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader("data.txt"))) { System.out.println(reader.readLine()); }
hint: The resource must implement AutoCloseable and is declared inside the parentheses after try.

front: Write a Java switch expression that assigns "WEEKEND" to result for SATURDAY or SUNDAY and "WEEKDAY" for any other DayOfWeek value named day.
back: String result = switch (day) { case SATURDAY, SUNDAY -> "WEEKEND"; default -> "WEEKDAY"; };
accepted_answers: String result = switch (day) { case SATURDAY, SUNDAY -> "WEEKEND"; default -> "WEEKDAY"; };
hint: Arrow-labeled switch expressions do not fall through and can be assigned directly.
